title: The Costa Concordia Took Sixty-Nine Minutes to Order Everyone Off the Ship.
title_candidates: The Costa Concordia Took Sixty-Nine Minutes to Order Everyone Off the Ship.
It Took Sixty-Nine Minutes to Give the Order to Leave.
Nearly Two Thousand Had Never Walked to Their Muster Station.
Three Numbers for the Same People.
description:
A cruise ship is a building that floats, and the thing that tells you a building is in trouble is the floor.

On a January night off the Italian coast, four thousand two hundred and twenty-nine people felt a floor stop being level. It took sixty-nine minutes to give the order to leave.

This is a film about what used up the sixty-nine minutes.

It is the thirteenth of January, 2012. There are four thousand two hundred and twenty-nine people on board — three thousand two hundred and six passengers and one thousand and twenty-three crew. A thousand crew is not a skeleton staff.

Of the three thousand two hundred and six passengers, one thousand two hundred and seventy had attended a muster: four hundred and sixty-three of them at Toulon, four hundred and fifty-six at Barcelona. The rules of the time allowed the briefing another way. It also meant that on the night this happened, nearly two thousand people on that ship had never once walked to their muster station.

At seven seconds past nine forty-five, the hull strikes the rock furthest east of Le Scole, on the left side. Fifty-one seconds later, the recorder captures the blackout. Seven seconds after that, the emergency generator starts. It runs for forty-one seconds. Then it stops being able to supply the ship's essential services continuously — and the two essential services named in the report are the rudder and the bilge pump.

Compartment five held the propulsion electric motors and the fire and bilge pumps. Compartment six held three of the main diesel generators. Those are the two the rock opened. So the water came in through the hole, and the two things that could have fought the water — the power and the pumping — were standing in the water.

The investigative body states it directly: no measure is sufficient to render the ship unsinkable when more than two contiguous watertight compartments are flooded.

What follows is a record of who was told what, and when. At thirty-four seconds past nine fifty-seven, the master informs the company's designated person ashore. At twelve minutes past ten, the public address makes its first announcement to the passengers. At twenty-five minutes and fifteen seconds past ten, the master tells Livorno there is a hull breach on the left side causing a gradual heel — that is forty minutes after the contact, and it is the first time the shore hears the word breach. At twenty-six seconds past ten thirty-three, the general emergency is announced, forty-eight minutes after the contact. At fifty-four minutes and ten seconds past ten, the abandon ship is ordered: sixty-nine minutes after the hull struck the rock.

And the angle of the ship is doing something the whole time. At thirteen degrees you can still walk, badly. At thirty the decks are ramps. At forty, which is where she was around midnight, walking is climbing. At eighty, where she ended, the corridors are shafts.

The investigators set out what a different timeline would have produced. Suppose the general emergency signal had been given at thirty-nine minutes past ten. On that timeline the abandon ship would have followed thirty-six minutes after the signal, and passengers would have started leaving the ship while she had thirteen degrees of heel.

Thirty-two people died. Twenty-six passengers and four crew are recorded as deceased. Thirty people were found; two were never found — one passenger, one crew member. A hundred and fifty-seven passengers claimed injuries.

—

Prime Documentary makes long-form documentaries about ordinary people and the systems that fail around them. This episode is built from the marine casualty investigation report. The Italian criminal proceedings are not covered here: that record has not been opened for this film, and no criminal outcome appears in it.

This film contains AI-assisted visualization: symbolic reconstruction, no real likenesses. Generated imagery is not evidence and is not presented as an authentic record.
